9.need-data: This stage uses your data and stages 1 to 8: load it and meet them first.

reads.title: What is read
reads.body: The test set isn't opened again: this stage reads what stage 8 measured on it and your costs from stage 1. No row of your data takes part.
reads.no-table: Stage 8 was recorded before it kept its threshold table, and without it there are no numbers to decide with. Go back to stage 8 and record it again: the test set is opened again, and it counts as a new opening only if the setup changed, labeled as such.

threshold.title: The threshold
threshold.costs: Your costs from stage 1 give a threshold of {umbral}: acting pays from that probability on (a false alarm costs {fp} and a case that slips through {fn}).
threshold.label: Threshold at which you act
threshold.help: Your costs' threshold is set without looking at the test set. If you move it reading the curve, the number you get is optimistic and it's labeled.
threshold.moved: Chosen while looking at the test set: optimistic.
threshold.reason-help: Why this threshold and not your costs' one. Up to {max} characters.
threshold.class: The winner gives no probabilities: it decides with the class it predicts. There's no threshold to move.

numbers.title: At this threshold
numbers.interval-note: The interval is stage 8's: it was measured at your costs' threshold.
numbers.saves: Against what you do today ({hoy}), the model saves {ahorro} per 100 decisions.
numbers.costs-more: Against what you do today ({hoy}), the model costs {ahorro} more per 100 decisions.
numbers.same: Against what you do today ({hoy}), the model costs the same.
numbers.quantile: With your costs, falling short costs {sub} per unit and overshooting {sobre}: what pays to aim at is the {cuantil} quantile, not the average.

capacity.title: What your team can handle
capacity.label: Out of 100 cases, how many can your team handle?
capacity.help: A whole number from 0 to 100. If the threshold raises more alerts, the extra ones go unattended.
capacity.fits: This threshold raises {alertas} alerts per 100 cases: your team can handle them.
capacity.exceeds: This threshold raises {alertas} alerts per 100 cases and your team handles {capacidad}.
capacity.threshold: Your capacity's threshold is {umbral}: it raises {capAlertas} alerts per 100 cases and costs {costo} per 100 decisions.

curve.title: The decision curve
curve.intro: Net benefit at each threshold, per 100 cases: the alerts that are right minus the false ones, weighted by what each costs at that threshold. «Doing nothing» is worth 0; where the model falls below «act on everyone» or below 0, it adds nothing.
curve.image: The decision curve as a chart; the table below has the same figures.

decision.title: Your decision
decision.legend: What do you do with the model?
decision.help: Not using it is a valid result: it's written down with its numbers.
decision.reason-help: In your own words: why this decision, with these numbers. Up to {max} characters.

field.razon_umbral: Your reason to move the threshold
field.capacidad: Cases out of 100 your team handles
